question: In India's Census 2011, the child sex ratio is defined as the number of females per 1,000 males in the 0–6 year age group, and it recorded a value of 914 girls per 1,000 boys — a decline from 927 in Census 2001.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is actually true. Census 2011 defined the child sex ratio as females per 1,000 males aged 0–6 years, recorded at 914 — a fall from 927 in 2001 — signalling ongoing sex-selective practices despite the PNDT Act.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The child sex ratio (CSR) specifically covers 0–6 years and was 914 in 2011 vs 927 in 2001, reflecting the impact of sex-selective abortion particularly after the expansion of affordable ultrasound in the 1990s.
